scope: Independent Windows Herdr startup, cancellation of incomplete startup, and exact-session reopen

validation.old_binary_regression: The two independent-startup and incomplete-kill regressions both failed with the old installed binary.

core_run.initial_observation_failure: The hosted reopen observation exceeded its old 20-second fixture cap while the backend was running and its Codex display had launched. Rechecked successfully using the installed build and unchanged 60-second product startup budget.

cases: native Codex host preserves its thread

validation.live_acceptance: See native-startup-incident-20261013.json: Claude waiting for input, Pi and Codex ready, then kill of the still-opening generation returned closed.
validation.scope_note: Reports with failures from intermediate diagnostic runs are preserved as history, not represented as current green validation. This is targeted validation, not a claim that the entire repository suite was run.

behavior: Slow or blocked terminal providers do not prevent the native Codex host from starting.
Later ready agents join through reload without replacing the existing host or native session.
Startup authority is persisted before resource allocation; kill cancels the recorded opener and closes only verified owned resources.
Missing initial authority is rejected rather than reconstructed from current configuration.
Reopen preserves verified history and refuses a different native session.
Backend readiness and interface readiness are reported separately; the default background startup budget remains 60000 ms.
limits: The original seventy-second Pi delay did not reproduce, so its original cause remains unidentified.
No paid model tasks or trust confirmations were submitted. Automatic callback routing is exercised by offline protocol fixtures.
The formal project remains closed. Application source, provider account configuration and unrelated workspaces were not changed.
